117:Prudent defaults: the blink phase comes from `jobs.FrameMsg`, and `WantsBlink()` is true only while a row action is in flight (`restarting` never blinks); the footer detail is `Running since 3 hr ago` (`Running for less than a minute` under a minute), `progressLine()` replaces `actionLine()` and does not repeat an action already named by the selected row; an action failure stays a footer `Error` (D5). Risk: the parser is not measured against a real podman. Details in `docs/architecture/network.md`.
159:Until now the router ran one spinner chain (`jobTickMsg`) that broadcast a full `ChangedMsg` (snapshot and frame) to every held view at 10 Hz. The story asks for one tick that animates every row, blinking at 1 Hz, without rebroadcasting the snapshot. Decisions: (1) *One chain, renamed "animation"* (D2; formerly D5's "spinner chain"): `animationTickMsg{seq, at}`, `ensureTick`, `handleAnimationTick`, `animationState`. Only the router builds a `jobs.FrameMsg`; a source test enforces it. (2) *Two cadences:* 100 ms while `Running() > 0` (footer and row spinners need the frame), 500 ms when the view on screen implements `BlinkingView` and `WantsBlink()` is true and motion is blink. Otherwise no chain. (3) *The phase is read from the tick's own time:* `blinkOn = (UnixMilli/500) % 2 == 0`, so every row reads the same phase from the same tick. (4) *`FrameMsg{Frame, RenderedFrame, Blink}`* goes to the view on screen only, on every tick and on entry (`switchView`). `Frame` and `RenderedFrame` leave `jobs.ChangedMsg`, which keeps the snapshot only and now goes to every held view on a registry change. This reverses the earlier "one message and not two" comment, on purpose: the compiler then lists every reader of the frame, which protects against a view whose spinner freezes. (5) *Level signal:* `App.Update` is now a wrapper (`a.update` is today's switch, unchanged, then `ensureTick`). `ensureTick` runs after every message: it starts a chain when one is needed, replaces a slower chain by bumping `seq` (never two chains), and lets a live chain die at its next tick when nothing needs it. (6) *`tea.Every`, not `tea.Tick`:* `tea.Every` fires on the clock's boundaries, so `(UnixMilli/500) % 2` alternates strictly. With `tea.Tick` the drift accumulates and one blink is skipped (a steady 1 s `●`). (7) *Only the view on screen is asked `WantsBlink()`*, not every held view as the story's R3 said. Reason: the frame goes to the view on screen only, so a chain kept alive for an off-screen view would animate nothing. Stricter than the story; reversible in one line. (8) *`motionStatic` is a router field until A-02:* `setMotionStatic(bool)`, zero value = blink. A-02 wires it from `app.motion`; nothing is read from YAML here. `app.motion` does not exist yet (no `Motion` in `internal/config`). (9) *`datatable.Animating()` is not added here:* it has no caller before the first `BlinkingView` (A-09b/A-10a/A-13/A-14), and it goes with it. (10) *Four row-animation chains stay outside the router, declared as exceptions until A-16:* `oci_resources/busy.go` (`AdvanceSpinner`, A-09b), `containers/update.go` (`AdvanceSpinner`, A-14), `netdiag/ports_model.go` (`portsSpinnerCmd`, A-12), the OCI registry browser's `tagScanSpinnerIdx` (A-09a). A test lists them as declared exceptions: a new site fails it, and a stale exception fails it too. Criterion 4 of the story is therefore met on the router side here, and application-wide in A-16 (Q2, option A). (11) *Redraw-cost measurement is an in-process test, not a terminal capture* (Q1, option A): `TestMeasureRedrawCost` in `internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go`, skipped unless `DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1`, runs a real `tea.Program` on the real router with `WithOutput(countingWriter)`, 120×40, for 10 s, and logs bytes per second for N = 0, 1, 20 blinking rows. The story named `TEA_TRACE`, which does not exist in Bubble Tea v1.3.10 (checked in the module source: no `TEA_TRACE`, no `os.Getenv`); the research document cited it from a page about another version. This measures what the renderer writes, not what a terminal shows over SSH; the real-SSH check stays with the A-06 checkpoint, where H2 is consigned. No view blinks before A-06, so the PR cannot show "20 blinking rows" in the real application. (12) *No ADR:* a lasting decision recorded here, per the project's convention. Hand-off: A-02 calls `setMotionStatic`; A-06 adds `SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` to `:jobs`; the first `BlinkingView` adds `datatable.Animating()`; A-16 absorbs the declared exceptions.
167:The story asks where an agent's tokens went. Decisions: (1) *Two tabs inside a session*, Agents and Breakdown, switched with `tab` (Rule 135 reserves `tab` for tabs, and this is one). Opening or closing a session resets to Agents and scroll 0. (2) *Colour-only bar.* The Breakdown column draws one glyph, the gauge's (`app.gauge_glyph`), in four colours; acceptance criterion 3 of S-10 ("four different glyphs, readable without colour") is replaced by "one glyph, four distinct role colours" (decided 2026-11-05). Why, as the user gave it: homogeneity with the other views (the containers load gauges draw the same glyph through `app.gauge_glyph`) and the design. The cost is accepted and written in Rule 122's fifth exception: with no colour (`NO_COLOR`, 16 colours, colour-vision deficiency) the bar only says "has tokens"; the exact figures stay in the In/Out/Cache columns and in the Breakdown tab. (3) *`Column.Spans(item) []Span`* in `datatable`: N coloured runs over a finished cell, same measure-first order as `Cut`/`TailStyle` (Rule 122); `Spans` wins over them and a column declaring both is rejected (`TestNoColumnDeclaresSpansWithCutOrTailStyle`). (4) *Four token roles* (`theme.TokenStyle`: input, output, cache write, cache read; theme keys `token_input`, `token_output`, `token_cache_write`, `token_cache_read`), checked by `internal/ui/theme/tokencolors_test.go` (`TestTokenColorsAreDistinct`, `TestTokenColorsContrastWithBackground`, `TestTokenColorsAreNotSeverityOrGaugeColours`, `TestEveryShippedThemeSetsTheTokenKeys`). (5) *Column place and drop order:* between Model and In; dropped after In and before Model (`Cache write`, `Est. cost`, `Cache read`, `In`, `Breakdown`, `Model`, `Duration`, `Tools`, `State`), with `YieldsToContent` (D93). (6) *Footer order:* filter bar, breadcrumb, tab row, blank line, message. (7) *Header on Breakdown counts the whole session* (`agentTable.Items()`), because the panel ignores the filter and the sort; on Agents it follows the filter. (8) *Percentages are of tokens, never of cost*; rounding residue to the largest line (orchestrator in the agent block, to match the Share column). Docs: `agent-usage.md`, `ui-components.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, in-app help.
171:The `Breakdown` bar made the agents table squeeze the Agent column (a 30-character type cut from 33 to 23 at 160 columns) instead of dropping an Optional column, because `solveWidths` cuts content before it drops anything. Decision: an Optional column carrying `YieldsToContent` is removed before a required content column (`SizingContent`, not Optional) is cut, but only while it is the column `drop()` would remove next (`dropAt`, shared by `drop` and `nextYields`); the drop order does not change, only when the next drop happens. Optional content columns (Model) are still cut first. Set on Cache write, Est. cost, Cache read, In and Breakdown, not on Model, Duration, Tools or State, so the activity columns still hold at 80 columns for real types. Rejected: a global "drop an Optional column before cutting any content" rule (measured over 2,822 solver inputs: 41 change in 7 tables, 3 agent tests red, Duration lost at 80 columns with `general-purpose`); `Protected` on the Agent column (loses Duration, and State/Tools for long types); flagging only the two `DropFirst` columns (the bar still cuts the type between about 106 and 145 columns). Consequence: the agents thresholds depend on the longest agent type (Breakdown at 106 with short types, 110 with `general-purpose`, 125 with a 30-character type). Rule 116 unchanged: the widths still sum to the interior. Docs: `ui-components.md`, `agent-usage.md`, Rule 116 in `tui-tables.md`.

Otherwise no chain. (3) *The phase is read from the tick's own time:* `blinkOn = (UnixMilli/500) % 2 == 0`, so every row reads the same phase from the same tick. (4) *`FrameMsg{Frame, RenderedFrame, Blink}`* goes to the view on screen only, on every tick and on entry (`switchView`). `Frame` and `RenderedFrame` leave `jobs.ChangedMsg`, which keeps the snapshot only and now goes to every held view on a registry change. This reverses the earlier "one message and not two" comment, on purpose: the compiler then lists every reader of the frame, which protects against a view whose spinner freezes. (5) *Level signal:* `App.Update` is now a wrapper (`a.update` is today's switch, unchanged, then `ensureTick`). `ensureTick` runs after every message: it starts a chain when one is needed, replaces a slower chain by bumping `seq` (never two chains), and lets a live chain die at its next tick when nothing needs it. (6) *`tea.Every`, not `tea.Tick`:* `tea.Every` fires on the clock's boundaries, so `(UnixMilli/500) % 2` alternates strictly. With `tea.Tick` the drift accumulates and one blink is skipped (a steady 1 s `●`). (7) *Only the view on screen is asked `WantsBlink()`*, not every held view as the story's R3 said. Reason: the frame goes to the view on screen only, so a chain kept alive for an off-screen view would animate nothing. Stricter than the story; reversible in one line. (8) *`motionStatic` is a router field until A-02:* `setMotionStatic(bool)`, zero value = blink. A-02 wires it from `app.motion`; nothing is read from YAML here. `app.motion` does not exist yet (no `Motion` in `internal/config`). (9) *`datatable.Animating()` is not added here:* it has no caller before the first `BlinkingView` (A-09b/A-10a/A-13/A-14), and it goes with it. (10) *Four row-animation chains stay outside the router, declared as exceptions until A-16:* `oci_resources/busy.go` (`AdvanceSpinner`, A-09b), `containers/update.go` (`AdvanceSpinner`, A-14), `netdiag/ports_model.go` (`portsSpinnerCmd`, A-12), the OCI registry browser's `tagScanSpinnerIdx` (A-09a). A test lists them as declared exceptions: a new site fails it, and a stale exception fails it too. Criterion 4 of the story is therefore met on the router side here, and application-wide in A-16 (Q2, option A). (11) *Redraw-cost measurement is an in-process test, not a terminal capture* (Q1, option A): `TestMeasureRedrawCost` in `internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go`, skipped unless `DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1`, runs a real `tea.Program` on the real router with `WithOutput(countingWriter)`, 120×40, for 10 s, and logs bytes per second for N = 0, 1, 20 blinking rows. The story named `TEA_TRACE`, which does not exist in Bubble Tea v1.3.10 (checked in the module source: no `TEA_TRACE`, no `os.Getenv`); the research document cited it from a page about another version. This measures what the renderer writes, not what a terminal shows over SSH; the real-SSH check stays with the A-06 checkpoint, where H2 is consigned. No view blinks before A-06, so the PR cannot show "20 blinking rows" in the real application. (12) *No ADR:* a lasting decision recorded here, per the project's convention. Hand-off: A-02 calls `setMotionStatic`; A-06 adds `SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` to `:jobs`; the first `BlinkingView` adds `datatable.Animating()`; A-16 absorbs the declared exceptions.
167:The story asks where an agent's tokens went. Decisions: (1) *Two tabs inside a session*, Agents and Breakdown, switched with `tab` (Rule 135 reserves `tab` for tabs, and this is one). Opening or closing a session resets to Agents and scroll 0. (2) *Colour-only bar.* The Breakdown column draws one glyph, the gauge's (`app.gauge_glyph`), in four colours; acceptance criterion 3 of S-10 ("four different glyphs, readable without colour") is replaced by "one glyph, four distinct role colours" (decided 2026-11-05). Why, as the user gave it: homogeneity with the other views (the containers load gauges draw the same glyph through `app.gauge_glyph`) and the design. The cost is accepted and written in Rule 122's fifth exception: with no colour (`NO_COLOR`, 16 colours, colour-vision deficiency) the bar only says "has tokens"; the exact figures stay in the In/Out/Cache columns and in the Breakdown tab. (3) *`Column.Spans(item) []Span`* in `datatable`: N coloured runs over a finished cell, same measure-first order as `Cut`/`TailStyle` (Rule 122); `Spans` wins over them and a column declaring both is rejected (`TestNoColumnDeclaresSpansWithCutOrTailStyle`). (4) *Four token roles* (`theme.TokenStyle`: input, output, cache write, cache read; theme keys `token_input`, `token_output`, `token_cache_write`, `token_cache_read`), checked by `internal/ui/theme/tokencolors_test.go` (`TestTokenColorsAreDistinct`, `TestTokenColorsContrastWithBackground`, `TestTokenColorsAreNotSeverityOrGaugeColours`, `TestEveryShippedThemeSetsTheTokenKeys`). (5) *Column place and drop order:* between Model and In; dropped after In and before Model (`Cache write`, `Est. cost`, `Cache read`, `In`, `Breakdown`, `Model`, `Duration`, `Tools`, `State`), with `YieldsToContent` (D93). (6) *Footer order:* filter bar, breadcrumb, tab row, blank line, message. (7) *Header on Breakdown counts the whole session* (`agentTable.Items()`), because the panel ignores the filter and the sort; on Agents it follows the filter. (8) *Percentages are of tokens, never of cost*; rounding residue to the largest line (orchestrator in the agent block, to match the Share column). Docs: `agent-usage.md`, `ui-components.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, in-app help.
171:The `Breakdown` bar made the agents table squeeze the Agent column (a 30-character type cut from 33 to 23 at 160 columns) instead of dropping an Optional column, because `solveWidths` cuts content before it drops anything. Decision: an Optional column carrying `YieldsToContent` is removed before a required content column (`SizingContent`, not Optional) is cut, but only while it is the column `drop()` would remove next (`dropAt`, shared by `drop` and `nextYields`); the drop order does not change, only when the next drop happens. Optional content columns (Model) are still cut first. Set on Cache write, Est. cost, Cache read, In and Breakdown, not on Model, Duration, Tools or State, so the activity columns still hold at 80 columns for real types. Rejected: a global "drop an Optional column before cutting any content" rule (measured over 2,822 solver inputs: 41 change in 7 tables, 3 agent tests red, Duration lost at 80 columns with `general-purpose`); `Protected` on the Agent column (loses Duration, and State/Tools for long types); flagging only the two `DropFirst` columns (the bar still cuts the type between about 106 and 145 columns). Consequence: the agents thresholds depend on the longest agent type (Breakdown at 106 with short types, 110 with `general-purpose`, 125 with a 30-character type). Rule 116 unchanged: the widths still sum to the interior. Docs: `ui-components.md`, `agent-usage.md`, Rule 116 in `tui-tables.md`.

## 1. Known defects

**Rien d'ouvert.** D59, D62 et D63 sont fermés le 2026-08-28, et **D64** — la
boîte Health rendant les certificats dans le vocabulaire des moniteurs, signalé
et corrigé le même jour — avec eux. **D65**, l'inventaire `:sec` affirmant
« Nothing scanned yet » avant d'avoir lu ses caches, a été signalé et fermé le
2026-08-29, et **D66** — la colonne CI rendant les mots de GitHub au lieu de
ceux de l'interface — le même jour. **D67** — un scan de `ws` reprenant l'écran

# DEVDESK-152 (A-14) — Containers: docker's observed states in the activity column

Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-14. UX: `ux.md` §1.1, §1.2 (footer
sentences), §2.4, §3.5 (mock-ups), §5 (legend, containers extension), §5 bis (last row: the help
in `view.go` is replaced). Decisions D7, D8, D9, D10.
Pattern: DEVDESK-150 (netdiag ports: a `busy` action only, no registry, `IndicatorColumn`,
`jobs.FrameMsg`, `WantsBlink`, guard seed driving the view's `Update` without running any `Cmd`),
DEVDESK-146 (OCI images: `DescribeRow` with `Observed: Running` for a busy row, rest icon by role).

**What makes this story M and not S.** Column 0 already exists with the right shape (untitled,
`SizingFixed`, `IconColumnWidth`), so the widths, Rule 116 and the gauges do not move. What is new
is the **observed** state: `docker.Container` has no exit code and no age today. `⊗` (exited
non-zero) and `⊖` (exited 0) cannot be told apart without one (criterion 3), and the footer
sentences of `ux.md` §1.2 need an age ("Running since 3 hr ago", "Exited with code 137 — 5 min
ago"). Where those facts come from is Q1.

Nothing goes through the registry: `jobs.ChangedMsg`, `jobs.ForgetTarget`, `FailureEvent` and the
failure memory are **not used**. An action failure stays a footer `Error` (criterion 4, D5).
Out of scope: moving the instant actions to the registry; the gauges; prune (not a row action, it
keeps its footer line).

## Blocking questions (user)

| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | **Where the exit code and the ages come from.** `docker ps` gives `State` and a human `Status` ("Up 3 hours", "Exited (137) 5 minutes ago", "Restarting (1) 3 seconds ago"). It has no exit-code, start-time or restart-count field (podman's `ps` does, docker's does not; the PS template is shared, `engine.go`). | **A** parse `Status` once in `internal/docker` (`ParseStatus`): exit code exact; age = lower bound of docker's rounded duration ("2 weeks" → 14 days, "About an hour" → 1 hr); no extra process; restart count unavailable, so "◕ Restarting — last exit code 1" without "4 restarts" (ux.md §1.2 allows it: "the exact labels depend on the data available") · **B** one `docker inspect --format '{{.Id}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.StartedAt}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' <ids…>` per list refresh: exact facts and the restart count, but one more subprocess every 2 s, a template to check under podman (§3.67), and a new failure path for the list · **C** show `Status` verbatim in the footer ("Running — Up 3 hours"): no parsing of durations, but the footer sentences validated in D10 change wording, and the exit code still has to be parsed for the column | **A**. The exit code is needed for the column in every option; A gets it from the line already fetched, and an age rounded the way docker rounds it is what the user would read in `docker ps` anyway. B costs a subprocess per refresh to make a footer exact to the minute. The plan is written for A; B replaces step 1 only. |
| Q2 | **Criterion 2: the rest icon of a `running` container and its `IconRole*`.** Today the running row shows `theme.IconCaretRight` (󰍟, "small play") in the default text colour, with no role (`containerStateStyle` returns an empty style). Rule 125 says an icon's colour goes through a role declared in `iconcolors.go`; Rule 122 says the nominal state is not coloured. | **A** `theme.IconContainer` (, the view's title icon: "the container type icon" of the story) + a new role `IconRoleContainer`, default `ColorText`, overridable by a new theme key `icon_container` like the other roles · **B** same new role, but keep `IconCaretRight` (the glyph users already know for "running") · **C** `IconContainer` with a new role that is **not** overridable (no theme key; `IconColor` returns `ColorText`) · **D** reuse `IconRoleImage` (default `ColorHighlight`): rejected below, listed for completeness | **A**: it is what the story's hypothesis names, the role keeps Rule 125's "every icon colour is a role, every role is overridable", and `ColorText` keeps the nominal row uncoloured (Rule 122). D would paint every running row yellow (colour discipline) and say "image" about a container. |
| Q3 | **States outside the vocabulary.** Docker also reports `removing`; podman can report `stopping`, `stopped`, `configured`, `initialized`, `unknown`. `stateToken` already files them (transient or stopped), the column has no glyph for them. | **A** `◌` (Unknown) + footer naming the state as reported ("◌ Removing"), legend label "created" extended to "created, or another state in transition" (amends D10 text) · **B** `◌` + footer naming the state, legend unchanged (the legend says "◌ created", the footer says the real state) · **C** map the podman synonyms first (`configured`/`initialized` → created `◌`; `stopped` → read like `exited`), then B for the rest | **C** (which includes B): the synonyms are the same states under another name, and the rest is rare and brief (a `removing` lasts a moment). No validated text changes. |
| Q4 | **The selected row of an `exited` code 0 container.** `containerSelectedStyles` paints the whole selected row red (`TableStylesForState("error")`) for `exited` **and** `dead`, so a container that stopped cleanly is red under the cursor while its glyph is a neutral `⊖` ("nothing to fix", ux.md §5 case 6). | **A** red row only for the `Failed` states (exited non-zero, dead, exited with an unknown code) · **B** unchanged (any `exited` and `dead`) | **A**: one meaning per state; ux.md §3.5 only shows the red row on `job-7` (exited 137). |
| Q5 | **Legend wording of the busy row.** The validated extension (D10, criterion 8, already in `indicator.ContainersLegend`) says "an action (stop, kill, remove) is running". This view has no kill: its row actions are stop, restart, pause, resume, delete, and all of them mark the row busy (`startAction`). | **A** keep the validated text · **B** "an action (stop, restart, pause, resume, delete) is running" (amends D10 and the text of criterion 8) | **B**: Rule 114 asks the help to describe this view, and a user pressing `K` is offered Stop / Restart, never Kill. A is acceptable if the wording is meant to be shared with another view (none uses this entry). |

## Hypotheses (prudent default, no question)

- H1 **Column 0** = `datatable.IndicatorColumn(observedState, restIcon, restStyle)` (step 2). Its shape
  is the one of today's column, so widths do not move: at 60 columns `RenderedWidth() == 58`, the
  gauges (`Cut`/`TailStyle`) are untouched. `columnStatus` is renamed `columnIndicator`.
- H2 **Observed state** (`observedState(c) indicator.State`), with Q1-A, Q3-C:
  `running` → `Idle`; `restarting` → `Restarting`; `paused` → `Suspended`; `created`, `configured`,
  `initialized` → `Unknown`; `exited`, `stopped` with exit code 0 → `Skipped`; `exited`, `stopped`
  with exit code ≠ 0 **or unknown** → `Failed` (a possible crash is never shown as clean); `dead` →

# DEVDESK-200 — The space key and the legacy key fields go through `internal/ui/keymap` (Charm v2 guard rails, S1)

Story: Plane DEVDESK-200. Context: `.claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md` §1 (silent breaks) and §4 (S1).
Base: `main` at `d869dcc` (DEVDESK-199 merged: every test key is built by `internal/ui/testutil`).

**Why.** In bubbletea v1 `KeyMsg.String()` of the space is `" "`; in v2 it is `"space"`. Nothing
detects the change: every `case " "` silently stops matching, and every checkbox of the application
stops toggling (Rule 135). The fix is one constant, `keymap.Space`, that every binding reads, plus a
source test that refuses the literal. The v2 migration then changes one line.

## Survey (recount on `d869dcc`)

**`case " "` in production: 12 clauses, in 12 files** (the impact study counted 21; the code moved
since, DEVDESK-145 to DEVDESK-218 rewrote several handlers). No `== " "` / `!= " "` against a key in
production. `internal/app` has none.

| # | File:line | Clause | What space does | Existing space test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `internal/ui/components/choice_modal.go:75` | `case "enter", " "` | picks the focused button | **none** |
| 2 | `internal/ui/components/confirm_modal.go:50` | `case "enter", " "` | confirms the focused button | `TestConfirmModalEnterAndSpaceConfirmSelection` |
| 3 | `internal/ui/components/option_confirm_modal.go:131` | `case " "` | toggles the checkbox, else confirms | `TestDeleteConfirmModalSpaceTogglesCheckboxWhenFocused` |
| 4 | `internal/ui/configuration/update.go:83` | `case " "` | `toggleField` (checkbox, reveal secret) | `TestOnlySpaceTogglesACheckbox` |
| 5 | `internal/ui/containers/update.go:171` | `case " "` | pause / resume | `TestSpaceTogglesPauseAccordingToState` |
| 6 | `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_model.go:381` | `case " "` | pause / resume the live list | `ports_model_test.go` (5 sites) |
| 7 | `internal/ui/netdiag/forward_model.go:312` | `case " "` | pause / resume a forward | `TestSpaceAsksTheRouterToToggleTheSelectedForward` |
| 8 | `internal/ui/oci_resources/launch_form.go:312` | `case " "` | toggles a port or option checkbox | **none** |
| 9 | `internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_keys.go:85` | `case " "` | toggles a registry / group | `TestSpaceTogglesTheFocusedRegistry` and 4 more |
| 10 | `internal/ui/security/remediation.go:530` | `case " "` | chooses the candidate | `remediation_write_test.go`, `remediation_signatures_test.go` |
| 11 | `internal/ui/setup/confirm.go:41` | `case "enter", " "` | confirms the selection | **none** |
| 12 | `internal/ui/forge/explorer/update.go:189` | `case " "` | ticks / unticks a row | `TestSpaceTicksTheRowAndTheCellFollows` |

5 of the 12 files do not import `keymap` yet: `choice_modal.go`, `confirm_modal.go`,
`option_confirm_modal.go`, `launch_form.go`, `setup/confirm.go`. `keymap` imports only `maps`,
`sort`, `strings`: no import cycle is possible.

**Legacy key fields in production** (outside `internal/ui/testutil`, which DEVDESK-199 made the one
place that builds keys and is out of scope): only two sites.

| File:line | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/app/command_line.go:34` | `switch msg.Type { case tea.KeyEsc / KeyTab / KeyShiftTab / KeyUp / KeyDown / KeyEnter }` | `switch` on the key name (step 4) |
| `internal/ui/filebrowser/form.go:104-115` | rebuilds `tea.KeyMsg{Type: keyTypeFor(key)}` from `"left"`/`"right"` to forward it to the textinput | forwards the original `msg`; `keyTypeFor` is deleted |

`.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`: **0** in production. The announced keys (`{Key: "space", …}` in 11
shortcut lists) are display strings, not comparisons: untouched (Rule 138 vocabulary; v2 makes the
binding and the label the same word, a later tidy-up).

**The keymap scanner today ignores `case keymap.X`.** `clausesOf` (`keymap_test.go:332`) keeps only
`*ast.BasicLit`. Once `" "` becomes `keymap.Space`, a switch whose only structural literal was `" "`
(`containers/update.go`'s normal-key switch has `"ctrl+r"`, so it survives, but nothing guarantees
the next one) would stop being recognised as a key switch, and its letters would leave the three
vocabulary tests silently. Criterion 5 is this: the scanner must read `keymap.Space` as `" "`.

**`TestMeasureRedrawCost` exists** (`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go`, DEVDESK-139, D96 §11):
opt-in (`DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1`), logs **bytes per second** only. Criterion 7 asks bytes **and
duration per redraw**: the test is extended (step 5), not created. In bubbletea v1.3.10
`standardRenderer.flush` writes once per frame (`standard_renderer.go:283`), so bytes per redraw =
bytes / `Write` calls; the program calls `View()` after every `Update`, so the duration per redraw
is the mean `View()` time.

## Blocking questions (user)

| # | Question | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | **`OptionConfirmModal` toggles its checkbox on `enter`** (`handleConfirm`, `focused == 0`), against Rule 135 ("Enter … must not toggle a checkbox"), and a test pins it: `TestDeleteConfirmModalEnterOnCheckboxTogglesInsteadOfConfirming`. Criterion 4 asks "existing toggle tests unchanged + a test that enter does not toggle". Both cannot hold on this modal. | **A** fix it here: `enter` on the checkbox does nothing (or moves focus to Yes), rewrite that test; a behaviour change inside a story meant to be neutral · **B** keep this story neutral: the "enter does not toggle" test targets the launch form (uncovered today, step 1); open a bug for the modal | **B**. DEVDESK-200 is a refactor whose value is "nothing changes"; a fix mixed into it is harder to review and to revert. The plan is written for B; A adds one step (step 1b below). |
| Q2 | **Space never reaches a text field in two forms.** `configuration/update.go:83` sends every space to `toggleField`, which returns without forwarding on a text field; `launch_form.go:312` does the same for Entrypoint, Env, Volumes, User, Extra ports. So a path with a space (`C:\Program Files\…`) or `sh -c "…"` cannot be typed. Criterion 6 says "typing identical". | **A** fix both here (forward the space to the input when the focused field takes text) · **B** keep identical, open one bug, and do **not** pin the current behaviour in a test (a test that pins a defect has to be rewritten by the fix) | **B**, for the same reason as Q1. Criterion 6 is then checked where space reaches a field today (step 1). |

## Hypotheses (prudent default, no question)

- H1 **Alt-modified keys in the palette keep their meaning.** `switch msg.Type` matches `alt+up`,
  `alt+enter`, `alt+esc` (the type ignores `Alt`); `switch msg.String()` would not. To keep criterion
  3's "no behaviour change", step 4 switches on `strings.TrimPrefix(msg.String(), "alt+")`, and
  characterization tests pin the alt variants first. A local helper in `internal/app`, not in
  `keymap`: one caller.
- H2 **The guard excludes `internal/ui/testutil/`.** `testutil.Key` accepts `" "` and `"space"` as
  **test input names** (`testutil.go:115`); it translates a name into a message and binds nothing.
  DEVDESK-199's `source_guard_test.go` already owns that package.
- H3 **The guard reads switches and `==`/`!=`.** `slices.Contains(keys, " ")`, map keys and
  `strings.EqualFold` are not seen; stated as a limit in the test's comment.
- H4 **Measurements go in a new decision entry `D110`** at the top of `docs/backlog.md` (the latest
  is D109, line 101), with the command, the machine (CPU, kernel, OS), `go version`, bubbletea
  v1.3.10 and the commit measured. The v2 story reruns on one machine both this commit and its own,
  so the baseline does not depend on the machine it was first taken on.
- H5 **Plans and test names in English** (Rule 307), like the other plans.

## Steps

Order: **1 → 2 → 3**, and **4** in parallel with 2–3 after 1 (different files, separate guard
test). **5** is independent (only `internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` + backlog). **6** (docs) last.

Each step ends with `mise run lint` and the targeted tests green; the PR ends with `mise run check`.

---

### Step 1 — Characterization tests: what space, enter and typing do today

**Goal.** A safety net for the sites without a test, before anything moves. These tests are written
against the current code and **pass on it** (characterization, not red/green); they must pass
unchanged after steps 3 and 4. Keys only through `testutil.Key` / `Type` / `Paste` (DEVDESK-199).

**Files (tests only).**

- `internal/ui/components/choice_modal_test.go` (new)
  - `TestChoiceModalSpacePicksTheFocusedButtonLikeEnter` (table, `key ∈ {"enter", " "}`):
    `NewChoiceModal(…, []string{"Stop", "Restart"})`, focus on index 1 → `ChoiceModalPickedMsg{Index: 1, Label: "Restart"}`;
    focus on Cancel (`len(choices)`) → `ChoiceModalCancelledMsg`. Read the constructor before writing.
- `internal/ui/setup/confirm_test.go`
  - `TestConfirmPromptSpaceConfirmsTheCurrentSelection`: same table as
    `TestConfirmPromptEnterConfirmsTheCurrentSelection`, key `" "`, same expected messages.
- `internal/ui/oci_resources/launch_form_keys_test.go` (new) — **criterion 4**
  - `TestLaunchFormSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox` (table over Remove, Detach, Interactive, first port):
    focus the field (`f.focusedField = f.fieldOptionRemove()` …, then `f.updateFocus()`), `" "` →
    value flipped, a second `" "` → flipped back.
  - `TestLaunchFormDetachAndInteractiveExcludeEachOther`: Detach on, then Interactive on → Detach off;
    and the reverse.
  - `TestLaunchFormEnterNeverTogglesACheckbox` (same table): `enter` on each checkbox → value
    **unchanged**, `focusedField` advanced by one (Rule 135: "ignored or advance"). Error message
    names the field and Rule 135.
  - Build the form with `NewLaunchForm("api:v1", []string{"80/tcp"}, nil, 120)`; read
    `launch_form.go:98` for the exact signature and how `ports` is filled.
- `internal/app/command_line_test.go` (or `command_palette_test.go`, wherever `commanding(t, …)` lives)
  - `TestPaletteKeysKeepTheirMeaningWithAlt` (table): for `up`/`alt+up`, `down`/`alt+down`:
    `sugCursor` moves the same way; `esc`/`alt+esc`: palette closed (`a.commandMode == false`);
    `enter`/`alt+enter` on `quit` typed: same result as `TestQuitCommandQuits`; `shift+tab`: input
    value unchanged; `tab` with a highlighted suggestion: input completed. Pins H1.

  `internal/ui/keymap/` and `internal/ui/testutil/` (H2, reason in a comment), reports each finding:

  code").

`case "enter", keymap.Space`; add the `keymap` import in the 5 files listed in the survey. No other
change in those switches. Comments that spell `" "` for the key (e.g. `launch_form.go:313`) say
"Space".

**Command.**
```
go test ./internal/ui/keymap ./internal/ui/components ./internal/ui/configuration ./internal/ui/containers \
  ./internal/ui/netdiag ./internal/ui/oci_resources ./internal/ui/security ./internal/ui/setup \
  ./internal/ui/forge/explorer -count=1
```
**Done when** the guard passes, `TestTheKeyScanReadsKeymapConstants` finds `Space`, every test of
step 1 and every pre-existing space test passes **unmodified** (`git diff --stat -- '*_test.go'`
shows only the files this plan creates or names), and
`grep -rn --include=*.go 'case .*" "' internal/ui internal/app | grep -v _test.go` is empty.

---

### Step 4 — The two legacy key sites (criterion 3)

**Depends on** step 1 only (parallel with 2–3: no shared file).

**Red first: `internal/ui/keymap/legacy_key_scan_test.go` (new).**
```go
// legacyKeyReads returns "path:line" for every use, in a production file, of a v1-only
// key field or key type constant: X.Runes, X.Alt, X.Paste, and tea.Key<Name> other
// than tea.KeyMsg and tea.Key.
func legacyKeyReads(fset *token.FileSet, path string, file *ast.File, teaName string) []string
```
- `teaName` is the local name of the `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` import (`tea` everywhere
  today; read it from `file.Imports` so an alias is not missed); a file without the import is
  skipped.

  `case tea.KeyEsc:`, `tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyLeft}` → findings; `tea.KeyMsg` as a type,
  `msg.String()`, a struct field `Type` of a non-key value (`c.Type == "ssl"`) → none.
- `TestNoProductionCodeReadsLegacyKeyFields`: same walk and exclusions as step 3. Red now with
  exactly `internal/app/command_line.go` (6 constants) and `internal/ui/filebrowser/form.go`
  (`tea.KeyLeft`, `tea.KeyRight`, `tea.KeyType` is a type — decide: flag `tea.KeyType` too, since it
  disappears in v2).

**Green.**
- `internal/app/command_line.go`:

  // paletteKey is the key's name without an alt+ prefix: the palette matched on
  // KeyMsg.Type, which ignores Alt, and keeps doing so (DEVDESK-200).
  func paletteKey(msg tea.KeyMsg) string { return strings.TrimPrefix(msg.String(), "alt+") }

**Independent.** Files: `internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go`, `docs/backlog.md`.

  duration and the number of calls (atomics: `View` and `Update` run on the program goroutine, but
  the test reads them from another).

three times; record the median per case.

**Depends on** 3, 4, 5.

|---|---|

Le plan est écrit dans `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/plans/DEVDESK-200-plan.md` : 6 étapes, plus une étape 1b si Q1 = A. Je n'ai rien modifié d'autre. Deux questions bloquantes concernent la story : en l'état, les critères 4 et 6 ne peuvent pas tenir tels quels sur toutes les vues.

## Questions bloquantes (à poser à l'utilisateur)
- **Q1. `OptionConfirmModal` : Entrée coche ou décoche la case**, contre la Rule 135. Ça passe par `handleConfirm` quand `focused == 0`. Le test `TestDeleteConfirmModalEnterOnCheckboxTogglesInsteadOfConfirming` fige ce comportement. Le critère 4 (tests de bascule inchangés + un test « Entrée ne bascule pas ») ne peut donc pas tenir sur cette modale.
  - **A** : corriger ici et réécrire ce test.
  - **B** : garder la story neutre ; le test Entrée porte sur `LaunchForm`, qui n'a aujourd'hui aucun test d'espace ni d'Entrée, et on ouvre un bug pour la modale.
  - **Reco : B.**
- **Q2. L'espace n'atteint jamais un champ texte** dans deux formulaires :
  - `configuration/update.go:83` : `case " "` appelle `toggleField`, qui rend la main sans transmettre l'espace au champ texte ;
  - `oci_resources/launch_form.go:312` : même chose pour Entrypoint, Env, Volumes, User et Extra ports.

  On ne peut donc pas saisir un chemin avec espace ni `sh -c "…"`.
  - **A** : corriger ici.
  - **B** : bug séparé, sans test qui fige le défaut.
  - **Reco : B.** Le critère 6 est alors vérifié là où l'espace passe aujourd'hui : WrappedInput, FilterBar, CreationForm et la palette.

## Constats
- **Recompte : 12 `case " "` en production**, dans 12 fichiers, et non 21 : le code a bougé depuis l'étude Charm v2. Il n'y en a aucun dans `internal/app`, ni aucun `== " "` sur une touche. Cinq fichiers n'importent pas encore `keymap` : `choice_modal.go`, `confirm_modal.go`, `option_confirm_modal.go`, `launch_form.go`, `setup/confirm.go`.
- **Champs de touche hérités (`.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`) : aucun en production** hors `internal/ui/testutil`. Il reste deux sites :
  - `internal/app/command_line.go:34` fait `switch msg.Type` sur `tea.KeyEsc`, `KeyTab`, etc. ;
  - `internal/ui/filebrowser/form.go:104` reconstruit `tea.KeyMsg{Type: keyTypeFor(key)}`.
- **Le scanner de `keymap_test.go` ignore les `case keymap.X`** : `clausesOf` ne lit que les littéraux. Une fois `" "` remplacé par `keymap.Space`, des switches pourraient sortir silencieusement des trois tests de vocabulaire. C'est le fond du critère 5 : le scanner doit lire les constantes keymap en analysant `keymap.go`.
- **`TestMeasureRedrawCost` existe déjà** (`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go`), mais ne logue que des octets par seconde. Il faut l'étendre pour obtenir les octets par redessin (un `Write` par flush en v1.3.10) et la durée moyenne de `View()`.

## Étapes
1. **Tests de caractérisation**, verts sur le code actuel :
   - choice modal, setup confirm ;
   - LaunchForm : l'espace bascule chaque case, Entrée ne bascule jamais (critère 4) ;
   - touches de la palette avec et sans `alt+` ;
   - texte saisi avec accents et espaces, puis collé (critère 6).
2. **`keymap.Space = " "`.** `structuralKeys` lit cette constante, `clausesOf` résout `keymap.X`, et un test de garde `testutil.Key("space").String() == keymap.Space` cassera à la migration v2.
3. **Garde source puis migration.** Le test `space_scan_test.go`, avec un détecteur testé sur des sources en mémoire, refuse `" "` et `"space"` dans un `case` ou un `==`/`!=` et signale `fichier:ligne`. Il est rouge sur les 12 sites, qui passent ensuite à `keymap.Space`.
4. **Garde `legacy_key_scan_test.go`** (refuse `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.Key*`), puis correction des deux sites. La palette fait son `switch` sur `strings.TrimPrefix(msg.String(), "alt+")` pour garder le comportement de `msg.Type`. Peut se faire en parallèle des étapes 2 et 3.
5. **Mesure de référence v1** (indépendante) : le test est étendu, lancé trois fois, et la médiane est consignée en **D110** dans `docs/backlog.md`, avec commande, SHA, machine et version de Go.
6. **Documentation** : `app-shell.md`, Rule 135 dans `.claude/rules/tui-forms.md`, une ligne dans `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, et D110.

## Fichiers
- **Production** : `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go`, les 12 fichiers du tableau du plan, `internal/app/command_line.go`, `internal/ui/filebrowser/form.go`.
- **Tests créés** : `internal/ui/keymap/{space_scan_test.go, legacy_key_scan_test.go}`, `internal/ui/components/{choice_modal_test.go, typed_text_test.go}`, `internal/ui/oci_resources/launch_form_keys_test.go`.
- **Tests modifiés** : `internal/ui/keymap/keymap_test.go`, `internal/ui/testutil/keys_test.go`, `internal/ui/setup/confirm_test.go`, `internal/app/command_line_test.go`, `internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go`.

## Hypothèses retenues
- On garde le sens des touches `alt+` dans la palette.
- La garde exclut `internal/ui/testutil`, qui ne fait que construire des touches à partir de noms.
- La garde ne voit pas `slices.Contains` ni les clés de map.
- La référence de mesure n'est pas liée à une machine : la story v2 relancera les deux commits sur la même.

Hors périmètre, à noter : la map `actionConstants` d'`announced_test.go` ne contient ni `Diagnose` ni `Jump`.
